answer.book: Volume III of Ussher's Whole Works (1625): a polemical work, An Answer to a Challenge made by a Jesuit in Ireland, with a dedication to James I, an epistle to the reader, twelve chapters answering the Jesuit's points, and a closing catalogue of the authors cited.

entries.title: An answer to a challenge made by a Jesuit in Ireland, wherein the judgment of antiquity in the points questioned is truly delivered, and the novelty of the now Romish doctrine plainly discovered. By James Ussher, bishop of Meath.
To his most sacred Majesty, James, by the grace of God King of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, Defender of the Faith, &c. &c.
Chap. I. A general answer to the Jesuit's challenge
Chap. III. Of the real presence
Chap. V. Of the priest's power to forgive sins
Chap. VII. Of prayer for the dead
Chap. VIII. Of Limbus Patrum; and Christ's descent into hell
Chap. IX. Of prayer to saints
A catalogue of the authors here alleged, disposed according to the order of the times, wherein they are accounted to have lived
